libbrillo: Add CRLF after last boundary marker For multipart HTTP messages, the last encapsulation boundary marker still needs a CRLF after the second -- (https://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc1341/7_2_Multipart.html). This is causing our crash servers to mark our crash uploads as "malformed true". BUG=chromium:968831 TEST=Uploaded crash report. Confirmed that "malformed true" was not appearing. Revert "UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btusb: driver to enable the usb-wakeup feature" This reverts commit 74f911a25030 ("UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btusb: driver to enable the usb-wakeup feature"). The reason is that this causes any inband communication from the btusb device to cause the system to wake up. We know that the BT controller could be scanning when we decide to suspend and will send in the results once the scan is complete, thus failing the suspend entry. Bluetoothd should be listening to powerd for suspend requests to handle this properly, but we've observed enough spurious wakes that something still isn't right. (Reverting this commit has the side effect that BLE mouse clicks do not wake up the system from suspend, but that is lesser price to pay than no going to suspend). This was previously done for 4.4 at: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromiumos/third_party/kernel/+/750073 Signed-off-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@google.com> Signed-off-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> BUG=b:128319712 TEST=system can go to suspend even though BLE mouse is connected / scan is running Change-Id: Ia40208bf3ba45d722e754c49dead41a8ccf4a519 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1520811 Commit-Ready: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Tested-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Justin TerAvest <teravest@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ARM: dts: rockchip: Add pin names for rk3288-veyron jaq, mickey, speedy This is like commit 0ca87bd5baa6 ("ARM: dts: rockchip: Add pin names for rk3288-veyron-jerry") and commit ca3516b32cd9 ("ARM: dts: rockchip: Add pin names for rk3288-veyron-minnie") but for 3 more veyron boards. A few notes: - While there is most certainly duplication between all the veyron boards, it still feels like it is sane to just have each board have a full list of its pin names. The format of "gpio-line-names" does not lend itself to one-off overriding and besides it seems sane to more fully match schematic names. Also note that the extra duplication here is only in source code and is unlikely to ever change (since these boards are shipped). Duplication in the .dtb files is unavoidable. - veyron-jaq and veyron-mighty are very closely related and so I have shared a single list for them both with comments on how they are different. This is just a typo fix on one of the boards, a possible missing signal on one of the boards (or perhaps I was never given the most recent schematics?) and dealing with the fact that one of the two boards has full sized SD. Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de> (cherry picked from commit d85b2ad35a2ab320b9c0530992ee532f10a6aeb2 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/mmind/linux-rockchip.git v5.3-armsoc/dts32) BUG=chromium:970483 TEST=dut-control rec_mode:on; crossystem recoverysw_cur TEST=dut-control rec_mode:off; crossystem recoverysw_cur TEST=dut-control fw_wp_vref:pp3300 fw_wp_en:on fw_wp_state:force_on; crossystem wpsw_cur TEST=dut-control fw_wp_vref:pp3300 fw_wp_en:on fw_wp_state:force_off; crossystem wpsw_cur TEST=Compare /sys/kernel/debug/gpio and /sys/kernel/debug/*/*/pinmux-pins Change-Id: I358fdb1f8f588dc2584cc15a3958061291a158b8 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1644067 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: ip_sockglue: Fix missing-check bug in ip_ra_control() In function ip_ra_control(), the pointer new_ra is allocated a memory space via kmalloc(). And it is used in the following codes. However, when there is a memory allocation error, kmalloc() fails. Thus null pointer dereference may happen. And it will cause the kernel to crash. Therefore, we should check the return value and handle the error.
